topic: AI certificates versus proof of skill: what a certificate shows, what employers and clients can check, and how to build visible proof with AI as a coach
audience: Professionals and job seekers who are collecting AI courses and certificates and want them to turn into work, a job or clients
goal: Keep the certificates, and build one piece of visible proof this month: a small real project, a short write-up and a place people can see it, using AI as a coach and never as a shortcut
notes: Mojeed Abisiga holds certificates himself: the Microsoft Professional Degree in Data Science, Celonis Analyst and Data Engineer, and the IBM Big Data Engineer Mastery Award. He has approved this essay; certificates are a start, proof is what gets you hired. [provided by Mojeed Abisiga for this piece]

Anthropic's learning site is called Claude Academy (academy.claude.com) and is free: you can browse without signing in, and a free Claude account saves progress and earns completion badges; no paid plan or work account is needed. [https://academy.claude.com/help/faq]

Completion badges are earned by passing a course's quizzes (every lesson quiz plus any final assessment), not by finishing lessons; retakes are unlimited, subject to a daily badge limit that resets at midnight US Pacific time. [https://academy.claude.com/help/faq]

Claude Academy says completion badges don't expire: they record that you completed the course as it existed when you took it, with the issue date on the verification page. [https://academy.claude.com/help/faq]

To share a badge: on Your journey, open it and choose Download PDF or Add to LinkedIn; each badge also has a public verification link that lets anyone confirm it's genuine (badges from private courses have none of these). [https://academy.claude.com/help/faq]

Academy completion badges are not certifications: Claude certification exams are a separate paid, proctored program delivered by Pearson, with credentials issued through Credly, available only to companies in Anthropic's partner program. [https://academy.claude.com/help/faq]

The old course site anthropic.skilljar.com closes in early December 2026; learners should import their history into Claude Academy with a Claude account using the same email, and save certificate PDFs before then. [https://academy.claude.com/help/faq]
Claude Academy's 'AI Fluency: Framework and foundations' course has 14 lessons, 1 quiz and takes 4 hr, with a completion badge. [https://academy.claude.com/courses]

Google AI Essentials takes under 5 hours, needs no experience, and has 5 modules; in the U.S. and Canada it costs $49 USD per month after a 7-day free trial, on Coursera. [https://grow.google/ai-essentials/]

Google says finishing AI Essentials earns a certificate from Google to share with your network and potential employers, calling it 'a concrete way to show current and future employers your competency in AI'. [https://grow.google/ai-essentials/]

Microsoft Applied Skills credentials are earned by completing interactive tasks that align to real work in a lab-based assessment; Microsoft says they show employers you can hit the ground running on critical tasks. [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/applied-skills/]

Microsoft's FAQ says role-based Certifications typically validate 4-6 skill sets, while product-based Applied Skills validate one specific skill set, and Applied Skills are not replacing Certifications. [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/support/applied-skills-faq]

WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 (January 2025; over 1,000 employers): AI and big data top the list of fastest-growing skills; two-thirds of employers plan to hire talent with specific AI skills; analytical thinking is the most sought-after core skill, essential for seven out of 10 companies. [https://www3.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf]

Microsoft and LinkedIn's 2024 Work Trend Index (survey of 31,000 people in 31 countries): 66% of leaders say they wouldn't hire someone without AI skills; 71% would rather hire a less experienced candidate with AI skills than a more experienced one without them. [https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/ai-at-work-is-here-now-comes-the-hard-part]

The 2024 Work Trend Index reported a 142x increase in LinkedIn members adding AI skills like ChatGPT and Copilot to their profiles. [https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/ai-at-work-is-here-now-comes-the-hard-part]

LinkedIn's Skills on the Rise 2026 says employers increasingly prioritise skills over degrees, job titles or linear career paths, and that one in five professionals globally say lacking the right skills makes job searching harder. [https://news.linkedin.com/2026/Skills-on-the-rise-2026]

LinkedIn says it does not want 'AI slop': low-effort, likely AI-generated content that sounds polished but lacks a clear point of view, unique perspective or substance; it judges whether content adds value, not how it was made. [https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a1481496]

LinkedIn urges members to review, edit and approve AI-assisted content, says you are responsible for everything you post, and recommends saying so when you relied heavily on AI. [https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a1481496]

Desktop path for a LinkedIn document post: Start a post > More > 'Add a document' icon > Choose file > add a title > Done > add a description > Post; LinkedIn advises converting files to PDF where possible. Document posts accept PPT, PPTX, DOC, DOCX and PDF up to 100MB and 300 pages, and viewers can download the document as a PDF. [https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a518909]
After uploading a LinkedIn document post you can edit the post's description but not the document itself. [https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a518909]
